one_pager.big_idea: Scientists share their verdicts in public, say honestly how sure they are, and answer questions with evidence; and after ten weeks we can see how much our own thinking has grown.
goals: I can present our claim, test, data and verdict clearly in a 2-minute talk, with a confidence level and its reason.
I can answer or ask a question from the floor using evidence, not opinion.

flow.what: Skills check papers (fresh copies of the Week 1 paper) are face down on every desk. Students sit, write name, class and date, tick 'Week 10' and do not turn over. Slide 1.

Teacher reads the instructions aloud, keeps time, gives a 5-minute warning and collects the papers at once into a labelled envelope; same rules as Week 1 (assessment/Skills_Check_Y9.md Section 0). Students work alone and in silence. Slide 2.

Teacher becomes the chair: welcomes the 'delegates', returns each group's report, gives out question cards, feedback slips and listener sheets, explains the rules and running order. Each student checks their talk part and which group they ask and give feedback to. Slides 3 to 4.

Groups 1 to 6 present standing at their own table, holding up the report graph: 2 minutes each (bell at 1 minute 45 seconds, stop at 2 minutes), then one question from the floor (about 30 seconds) from the group before. Listeners tick each verdict and confidence. Teacher records strand 6 on the marking grid. Slides 5 to 7. If short: 90 seconds and no question for the last groups.
Students finish one two stars and a wish slip for the assigned group and hand it over, while the teacher collects the verdicts onto the verdict wall poster. Slide 8.

flow.phase: Interest survey and certificates (Think and Reflect)
flow.what: Teacher reads the survey statements aloud (3 min), then presents certificates and closes the series (2 min). Slides 9 to 10. The survey is fixed; certificates can move to the next session or an assembly.

one_pager.practical: No practical. Each group gives a 2-minute talk from its table using the talk frame and its fact-check report graph (claim, test, data, verdict with confidence, limits), then answers one question from the floor. Groups show graphs and photos, not practical kit.
one_pager.assessment: Final skills check (same paper as Week 1, 20 marks) into tracker column S, growth in column T; interest survey into columns U to Z; rubric strand 6 (Communicating) from the conference marking grid, strands 1 to 5 from the report and supporting evidence, all six into columns AC to AH; awards and certificates from assessment/Rubric_and_Reporting.md Section 3. Feedback slips are not marked but can support strand 5. No exit ticket or logbook line is required.
hazards: No practical hazards beyond normal classroom rules.
Groups show graphs and photos, not practical kit: no ice, warm water or fizzy drinks at the conference.
Questions and feedback are about the science, never the people or their English.
one_pager.language_note: Talk frame on every table and on slide 5; students may hold it and read from it. The rubric judges the clarity of the science, not the English. Answer frames: 'Good question. Our data shows ___.' 'We did not test that, but we think ___ because ___.' 'That could also be explained by ___.' 'To find out, we would need ___.' Chinese is welcome while groups prepare in the opening and on feedback slips; talks and questions are in English with key words, and a stuck student may say one sentence in Chinese and then the key word in English. Skills check: the teacher may read a question aloud and explain everyday words, but not science words; Chinese answers are accepted for explanations. Traps: a 'conference' is not a lesson; 'the floor' means the audience, not the ground; 'confidence' means how strong the evidence is, not how confident the speaker feels.
watch_out: Keep the skills check first and strictly timed (15 minutes) and the survey fixed (3 minutes): they measure growth. Do not go through the answers in this lesson.
Talks run late if groups change over slowly: groups present from their own tables and the next group stands as soon as the bell goes.

'Not enough evidence yet means our project failed': say in the opening that it is an honest and respected verdict. A question from the floor is not an attack, and confidence is not the same as the verdict ('Supported, low confidence' is possible).
Award levels need strand 6 from today's talk: have both possible certificates ready for boundary students. Most Improved Scientist waits until the skills checks are marked.
one_pager.next_week_link: End of the series: there is no Week 11. Use the close-out checklist (6f): within one week mark the skills checks, enter the tracker data, confirm strand levels and awards, decide Most Improved Scientist and print remaining certificates; then write the skills reports, add class figures and photos to the programme summary, run the gallery walk of reports, file the papers, return logbooks and return the kit to the prep room. Week 1 and Week 10 papers may be returned or discussed only now.
